osaka_ohlala_w_osaka.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information on the menu. Tabelog lists allergy information as available. Lunch and dinner centre on all-you-can-eat bread, pasta, steak frites and desserts (official menu).
osaka_ohlala_w_osaka.vegan_detail: Some vegan options: the à la carte menu has a vegan section — vegan burger, vegetable pasta, minestrone, green salad with vegan chicken, sautéed seasonal vegetables (official menu). Tabelog also lists vegetarian options. Courses are not vegan.
osaka_ohlala_w_osaka.hours_raw: Daily breakfast 7:00–11:00 (last order 10:45, buffet), lunch 12:00–15:00 (last order 14:00; lunch bookings limited to 90 minutes), dinner 17:30–22:00 (last order 21:00) (official site; Tabelog lists lunch and dinner). Reservations taken; no seat requests; seat selection unavailable at weekends and holidays (Tabelog). Tabelog says Marriott Bonvoy benefits and discounts do not apply; an October 2026 hotel guest says a Marriott member discount was given. À la carte unavailable on 19, 20, 24, 25 and 31 December 2026 (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and transport IC and other e-money; no QR. 160 seats; non-smoking; wheelchair accessible; kids menu; smart casual (Tabelog; official site).
osaka_ohlala_w_osaka.notes: [French · Minamisemba, W Osaka's brasserie on Midosuji] The all-day French brasserie on the third floor of W Osaka, opened March 2021, with big windows over the tree-lined Midosuji and a white, black and blue room with polka-dot touches. Lunch is the popular buy: courses with unlimited bread brought to the table and unlimited desserts. Most 2026 diners loved the bread and the lasagna; some found the single pasta choice limiting, the salad salty or the desserts samey. Dinner centres on steak frites, cooked rare and served with butter or sauce, against the night view. One October 2026 diner writes that the menu was developed with Chef Yusuke Takada of La Cime and the W Osaka chefs. The menu has a vegan section.

roles: Hotel kitchen team unnamed; breads and desserts by the W Osaka pastry and bakery chefs (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: A restaurant of W Osaka, opened 16 March 2021 (Tabelog). The official site describes traditional French cooking fused with Japanese ingredients and a modern sensibility, and playful presentation; the name is what the French say when surprised or excited. An October 2026 diner writes that the menu is developed by Chef Yusuke Takada of the two-Michelin-star La Cime together with the W Osaka executive chef team; no other source checked here says so.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Traditional French fused with Japanese ingredients and a modern sensibility" (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Steak frites; all-you-can-eat bread and desserts.

anecdotes.text: "The staff regularly came around with fresh bread, and for dessert, we could order from the menu without having to move at all, which was a nice touch." — October 2026, weekday lunch.
"The main dish is only a daily pasta special, so I would have been happier if there were a few more options." — September 2026.
"In the evening, you can enjoy the beautiful night view of Osaka through the large windows, adding a special touch to the hotel dining experience." — October 2026, steak frites course.
"As a Marriott member, I also received a discount." — October 2026, hotel guest (Tabelog says Marriott Bonvoy discounts do not apply).

osaka_ura_namba_sakana_ebisu.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Nigiri with red-vinegar rice and sashimi with soy and ponzu, plus fried shrimp, tempura, natto rolls and shumai; nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_ura_namba_sakana_ebisu.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood and sushi izakaya; the miso soup is aosa seaweed in a fish stock.
osaka_ura_namba_sakana_ebisu.hours_raw: Mon–Fri and the day before a holiday 16:00–23:30; Sat, Sun and holidays 12:00–23:30; last food order 23:00 (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; two-hour limit when busy; walk-ins at 18:30 on a Saturday were told to wait until about 20:00 (Tabelog; July 2026). Happy hour early in the evening (2026 reviews). Appetiser ¥399 (August 2026). Cards (VISA, Master) and PayPay (Tabelog). 35 seats with counter, sofas and a terrace; e-cigarettes only (Tabelog). The entrance is easy to miss (September 2026).
osaka_ura_namba_sakana_ebisu.notes: [Sushi izakaya · Ura-Namba, cheap nigiri and seafood plates] A lively sushi izakaya in Ura-Namba, the bar-and-small-plates sister of the Sushi Ebisu sushi shops in Tokyo and Kobe, with red-vinegar nigiri from ¥99 and long lists of seafood dishes under ¥1,000. Order the five-kind sashimi platter, the "Shrimp and Crab Battle" served on a crab shell, the sesame wasabi squid and a few nigiri, with sake from ¥399 a half-go. It fills up: come at the 16:00 opening (12:00 at weekends) for happy hour, or book. Expect ¥3,000–6,000 a head in 2026.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: the popular sister restaurant of Sushi Ebisu in Ebisu, Tokyo and Sannomiya, Kobe, opened in Ura-Namba; Edomae nigiri made with red vinegar in the Edo-period way, from ¥99; sake from ¥399 a half-go. Search results date the opening to January 2022 (not opened).
chef_bio.specialty: Red-vinegar nigiri; "Shrimp and Crab Battle".

anecdotes.text: "I overheard that guests without reservations arriving after us were told they would have to wait until around 8 PM." — July 2026, a Saturday at 6:30 PM.
"Under the crab shell in the shrimp and crab battle, I found yuzu pepper rolls" — September 2026, a first visit.
"The entrance was a bit hard to find, and we walked past it a couple of steps..." — September 2026, a daytime drink.

osaka_tsuchi_namba.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The menu is French toast, open sandwiches, mille-feuille and parfaits, with brunch plates of vegetables and chicken in sauce served with bread; the acai bowl and smoothies are the items without obvious wheat, but nothing is stated about them.
osaka_tsuchi_namba.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. There is soy milk for lattes (August 2026) and an acai bowl and fruit smoothies; the French toast, parfaits and plates use dairy, eggs or chicken.
osaka_tsuchi_namba.hours_raw: Daily 9:00–17:00, last order food 16:00, drinks 16:30; closed irregularly (Tabelog). Reservations accepted for tables; a booking needs one food item and one drink per person, no seat-only or drinks-only bookings; nine or more by phone (Tabelog). 90-minute limit (August 2026). Order and pay by QR code at the table; cash also accepted (September–October 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), transport IC, iD, QUICPay and PayPay (Tabelog). 36 seats inside and 30 on a terrace; non-smoking (Tabelog).
osaka_tsuchi_namba.notes: [Café · Namba, brunch in a hotel] A high-ceilinged brunch café on the ground floor of Hotel Royal Classic Osaka, beside Osaka-Namba Station, built on the Australian café model: specialty coffee, vegetable-heavy brunch plates and homemade French toast, served all day. The seasonal fruit is the draw: peaches in summer and figs in autumn 2026, in parfaits, French toast, mille-feuille and sodas. Order by QR code; a booking needs a food and a drink each, and stays are 90 minutes. Expect ¥2,000–3,000 a head; reserve at weekend lunch.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: "Bringing you a farm to table lifestyle from Tsuchi"; the new Tsuchi embraces Australian café culture, with high-quality coffee and meals in a comfortable space, brunch plates and sweets all day. An October 2026 regular notes the menu is gradually expanding and a pasta set has gone.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fruit French toast and parfaits; vegetable brunch plates.

anecdotes.text: "The seasonal mille-feuille always uses delicious fruits, and the figs were perfectly ripe and incredibly tasty." — October 2026.
"It's a prepay system, so I ordered and paid through a QR code while seated." — September 2026, the fig fair.
"for online reservations, it was mandatory to order both a drink and a dessert per person." — September 2026.

osaka_wa_french_baru_sonjuku_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a meat-led menu of beef, pork, foie gras and seafood, with a dashi omelette; bagna cauda vegetables are the main plant dish mentioned.
osaka_wa_french_baru_sonjuku_shinmachi.hours_raw: Daily 17:30–3:00, last order 2:30; open through Golden Week and Obon; lunch suspended; open all year, New Year to be confirmed (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, advisable as it is often busy; seat type not guaranteed (Tabelog; September 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money, PayPay and Rakuten Pay (Tabelog). 37 seats: 13 at the counter, 24 at tables; heated tobacco only indoors until 23:00, smoking on the terrace (Tabelog).
osaka_wa_french_baru_sonjuku_shinmachi.notes: [French-Japanese bar · Shinmachi, until 3 a.m.] A late-night bistro bar by Yotsubashi Station where a chef from a long-established Kyoto hotel mixes Kyoto and French cooking, in a room styled like a late-Edo townhouse. Order the beef sirloin wrapped in puff pastry (¥990 in June 2026) that regulars insist on, the dashi omelette, foie gras and an eight-item appetiser plate, with an inexpensive glass of wine. Open every night until 3 a.m.; a ¥4,980 course with drinks suits groups. A sister of イタリアン チャイナバル村塾 in Namba, different concept.

roles: Chef formerly of a long-established Kyoto hotel, unnamed (Tabelog shop text)

osaka_table_36_swissotel.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. The buffet includes seasonal vegetable salads and fruit, but most dishes are built on meat, seafood or dairy.

osaka_table_36_swissotel.notes: [Buffet and steak · Namba, 36 floors up] The restaurant of Swissotel Nankai Osaka on the 36th floor, straight above Nankai Namba Station, known for its lunch buffet and the view over the city from 147 m. The weekday buffet (¥5,900 in autumn 2026) runs from international dishes and a live kitchen of carved meats to some 30 desserts that diners return to again and again; breakfast and steak dinners with live music at weekends are the other draws. Book a window table; take the lift to the 6F lobby, then on to 36F. One October 2026 diner found the floor short of staff.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: a lunch buffet and dinner with views from 147 m above ground, directly connected to Namba Station, an open kitchen, American-style à la carte and premium steaks at dinner, live performances on Friday to Sunday. A July 2026 breakfast diner notes the hotel belongs to the Accor group.
chef_bio.specialty: Lunch buffet with live kitchen and desserts; wagyu and tomahawk steaks.

osaka_kitashinchi_kuroneko.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The courses include a hot pie, a zeppole that tastes like takoyaki, bread with butter and a black tantanmen as one meat choice; fish, meat and dessert are chosen from several options.
osaka_kitashinchi_kuroneko.vegan_detail: Not vegan: set courses of fish, meat (duck, wagyu, foie gras, pork) and dessert; the soup is a potage; no vegetarian course is mentioned.
osaka_kitashinchi_kuroneko.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–14:30 and dinner 18:00–22:00, Mon, Tue and Thu–Sun; closed Wednesdays and the first and third Tuesday of the month (reservations can be made for closed days) (Tabelog). One drink per person required; no service charge (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 14 seats: a counter of 9 and a private L-shaped counter room for 3–5; whole-shop hire up to 20; non-smoking; wheelchair users asked to call ahead; children welcome (Tabelog). A queue had formed before the 12:00 opening (September 2026).
osaka_kitashinchi_kuroneko.notes: [French · Kitashinchi, a creative course with a cat theme] A basement counter in Kitashinchi full of black-cat figurines, where the chef cooks a free-style French course that also borrows from Italian, Japanese and Chinese cooking. Each course opens with a pumpkin potage you scatter with homemade popcorn, then a 'palette' of small, intricate starters, among them a zeppole that tastes like takoyaki, before you pick a fish, a meat (the Hungarian duck with glazed apples is the favourite, foie gras extra) and a dessert such as the autumn parfait. Lunch from about ¥5,300, dinner ¥6,900. Anniversaries are a speciality: message plates and a black-cat whole cake. In October 2026 two men did all the cooking and serving. osaka_hortensia_bistro_higashimikuni.notes: [French · Higashimikuni, a bistro with game on the menu] A small, bright French bistro two minutes from Higashimikuni Station, with sofa seats and a little terrace, known for its game: Kagoshima badger with foie gras, Spanish mountain quail, rabbit wrapped around shrimp in the ¥8,800 Menu Hortensia (May and September 2026). Dishes are explained with care, and there is a good wine list; one drink each or a ¥1,000 seat charge. No preschool children at dinner. Closed Monday; Wednesday dinner only.

osaka_hillman_namba.notes: [Singaporean · Ura Namba, Hillman's paper chicken in Osaka] The Osaka branch of Singapore's Hillman Restaurant, upstairs on an Ura Namba back street since 2014 (an older Kitashinchi branch has closed, a September 2026 diner notes). A roomy, stylish space for groups, with all-you-can-drink courses and a ¥2,200 weekend lunch course. Diners in 2026 were mostly pleased; one found the appetizer plate poor value. Find the entrance from Sen’nichi Jizoson-dori. Open evenings daily, plus weekend lunch.

osaka_micasadeco_cafe_namba.notes: [Café · Namba, the original ricotta "dancing pancake"] The first Micasadeco&Cafe, opened in 2013 beside Namba Hatch, where the brand's ricotta pancakes became known as "dancing pancakes" for the way the three tall, wobbly layers arrive at the table; the site says the ricotta pancake won three stars at the SARAH Japan Menu Award 2018 for Kansai pancakes. They are made to order (about 20 minutes), light and only lightly sweet, at ¥1,750; there are chewy plain pancakes, seasonal specials, brunch plates and pasta too, and a morning menu here from 9:00. The queues of the pancake boom have gone and you can usually walk in, order from your phone and stay a while. A 2026 regular and others note that nearly all the guests, and some staff, come from overseas, which the site says is the target. Open daytime only, closed over the New Year.

osaka_dining_stage_sakaiya_asahi_namba.notes: [Izakaya · Namba, the relocated Sakaiya of croquette lunches] A basement seafood izakaya across the road from Takashimaya that many diners know as the old Sakaiya, a popular Namba lunch spot that closed and has reopened here as DINING STAGE Sakaiya Asahi ('the location and owner have moved and reopened', an October 2026 reviewer writes). The fist-sized croquettes are back: nikujaga or a seasonal cream croquette, on a set or a one-plate lunch with many small sides and free refills of rice. At night it is sashimi, big tempura prawns, fried oysters and chicken tataki, with all-you-can-drink courses. Returning regulars are split: some are delighted it survived, others find the lunch smaller and the grilled fish and rice weaker than before (October 2026). Open daily for lunch and dinner.

Book by the day before, especially on Fridays; a reservation assumes at least ¥2,500 a head, and a no-show after 15 minutes may be cancelled; seat-only or drinks-only bookings carry a ¥350 charge, not on courses (Tabelog). Cards for bills of ¥3,500 (before tax) or more, not with all-you-can-drink or discounts; PayPay and LINE Pay (Tabelog). 38 seats including a raised tatami area for 14; smoking allowed (after 13:00 at lunch, June 2026); up two flights of stairs (October 2026). Order by QR code (2026). Opened 29 September 2008 (Tabelog).
osaka_dogyan_honten_bakuromachi.notes: [Yakitori · Bakuromachi, Miyazaki chicken and a TV-famous ramen] Up two flights of stairs east of Shinsaibashi-suji, a casual Miyazaki izakaya open since 2008, with a counter, tables and a raised tatami area, where smoking is allowed. The draw is Miyazaki chicken: charcoal-grilled thigh of long-raised hens, chicken nanban under tartar sauce, fresh chicken sashimi and tataki. Yet many come for the ramen, five kinds, led by a Takaida-style chuka soba the shop calls its most popular dish (rich soy sauce on chicken broth, thick noodles) and a rare-in-Kansai Tsubamesanjo backfat ramen. Weekday lunch sets from ¥950 come with free refills of rice and miso soup. Diners in 2026 praise the chicken and the ramen; one found the lunch chicken nanban tough and pricey, another the floor greasy. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site (dogyan.jp): Miyazaki regional cuisine, charcoal yakitori and ramen at this main shop and a shop in 立売堀, Nishi-ku; the same group runs the noodle and kakigori shop 麺とかき氷 ドギャン 谷四店 (osaka_men_to_kakigori_dogyan_tanimachi in data). Per the Tabelog shop text: Miyazaki dishes such as charcoal-grilled thigh of long-raised hens, chicken nanban and meat-wrapped rice balls, plus the Takaida-style chuka soba, featured on TV several times and the most popular dish. Opened 29 September 2008 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal-grilled hen thigh; chicken nanban; Takaida-style chuka soba.

"I debated between Takai-da style and Tsubamesanjo style, but opted for the rare Tsubamesanjo style in Kansai." — June 2026, weekday lunch.
"This chicken cutlet had a good texture but was quite tough." — October 2026, Miyazaki chicken nanban set ¥1,100.
